title: Genesis 39: Joseph in Potiphar's House
body:
Read the chapter → [Genesis 39](/bible/genesis/39)

**[Genesis 39:1-6](/bible/genesis/39#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/genesis/39#v1)</sup> And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/genesis/39#v2)</sup> And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/genesis/39#v3)</sup> And his master saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/genesis/39#v4)</sup> And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/genesis/39#v5)</sup> And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/genesis/39#v6)</sup> And he left all that he had in Joseph’s hand; and he knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat. And Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured.

- The Lord was with Joseph in his captivity, and his master saw that the Lord made all that he did to prosper; Potiphar made him overseer over his house, and the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake.
- The Most High deals with His people even in captivity and gives them compassion before them who carried them captive; the favor on Joseph is the pattern of that prayer.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Kings 8:50](/bible/1-kings/8#v50)**
    > <sup>[50](/bible/1-kings/8#v50)</sup> And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions wherein they have transgressed against thee, and give them compassion before them who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them:

    Give them compassion before them who carried them captives; the Lord gave Joseph that compassion in Egypt.

**[Genesis 39:7-9](/bible/genesis/39#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/genesis/39#v7)</sup> And it came to pass after these things, that his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/genesis/39#v8)</sup> But he refused, and said unto his master’s wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand;
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/genesis/39#v9)</sup> There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?

- His master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, Lie with me; and he refused: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
- Adultery was known as sin from the beginning, long before Sinai. Abraham kept the commandments, statutes, and laws; and Abimelech rebuked Isaac because one of the people might have lain with his wife and brought guiltiness upon them. The nations themselves knew adultery brought guilt.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 26:5](/bible/genesis/26#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/genesis/26#v5)</sup> Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

    Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws; the laws are nothing new.
  - **[Genesis 26:10](/bible/genesis/26#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/genesis/26#v10)</sup> And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might lightly have lien with thy wife, and thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.

    Abimelech knew lightly lying with another man's wife would have brought guiltiness upon them; adultery was known sin.

**[Genesis 39:10-12](/bible/genesis/39#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/genesis/39#v10)</sup> And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/genesis/39#v11)</sup> And it came to pass about this time, that Joseph went into the house to do his business; and there was none of the men of the house there within.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/genesis/39#v12)</sup> And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.

- She spake to Joseph day by day, and he hearkened not. Then she arranged the empty house, caught him by his garment, and he left his garment in her hand and fled.
- That is the example: flee from sin as from the face of a serpent, for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee; the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion. Joseph knew thirty more seconds of entertaining her would be the bite.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 21:1-2](/bible/sirach/21#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/sirach/21#v1)</sup> My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for thy former sins.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/sirach/21#v2)</sup> Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.

    Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent; come too near and it will bite thee. Joseph fled.

**[Genesis 39:13-18](/bible/genesis/39#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/genesis/39#v13)</sup> And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth,
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/genesis/39#v14)</sup> That she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice:
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/genesis/39#v15)</sup> And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled, and got him out.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/genesis/39#v16)</sup> And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/genesis/39#v17)</sup> And she spake unto him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me:
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/genesis/39#v18)</sup> And it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled out.

- When she saw he was fled, she lied and cried that the Hebrew came in to mock her, holding his garment as evidence.
- The scriptures warn of that spirit: the woman whose heart is snares and nets and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter, and her ways are moveable; the same mouth that flattered turns and accuses.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiastes 7:26](/bible/ecclesiastes/7#v26)**
    > <sup>[26](/bible/ecclesiastes/7#v26)</sup> And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.

    The woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands; whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her, as Joseph escaped.
  - **[Proverbs 5:3-6](/bible/proverbs/5#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/proverbs/5#v3)</sup> For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/proverbs/5#v4)</sup> But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/proverbs/5#v5)</sup> Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/proverbs/5#v6)</sup> Lest thou shouldest ponder the path of life, her ways are moveable, that thou canst not know them.

    The lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, but her end is bitter as wormwood; her ways are moveable.

**[Genesis 39:19-20](/bible/genesis/39#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/genesis/39#v19)</sup> And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spake unto him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his wrath was kindled.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/genesis/39#v20)</sup> And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.

- When his master heard the words of his wife, his wrath was kindled and he put Joseph into the prison. He did not seek understanding, for jealousy is the rage of a man: he will not spare in the day of vengeance, nor regard any ransom.

  Precepts:
  - **[Proverbs 6:32-35](/bible/proverbs/6#v32)**
    > <sup>[32](/bible/proverbs/6#v32)</sup> But whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul.
    >
    > <sup>[33](/bible/proverbs/6#v33)</sup> A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.
    >
    > <sup>[34](/bible/proverbs/6#v34)</sup> For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
    >
    > <sup>[35](/bible/proverbs/6#v35)</sup> He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.

    Jealousy is the rage of a man; he will not spare in the day of vengeance nor regard any ransom; that is why no plea could reach Potiphar.

**[Genesis 39:21-23](/bible/genesis/39#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/genesis/39#v21)</sup> But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/genesis/39#v22)</sup> And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison; and whatsoever they did there, he was the doer of it.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/genesis/39#v23)</sup> The keeper of the prison looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper.

- But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison, and everything in the prison was committed to Joseph's hand.
- Everywhere Joseph went the favor followed, because the Most High was ordering his steps the whole way, so that Joseph would stand where he could save the whole house of Israel alive.
